question: Why is the na-to-pha Malini regarded as the primary form among the many divisions taught in scripture?
premises: Malini is sung in many divisions in the scriptures.
The na-to-pha form is the primary Malini.
As the inner, uncontracted state of Bhairava who is the mass of sound, she underlies those divisions.
inference: The primary Malini is the inner, expansive sound-form of Bhairava from which the various scriptural divisions arise.
uncertainties: Anucchūnatā is a technical term suggesting uncontracted fullness; the gloss is approximate.
The relation between Bhairava and the sound-mass is doctrinally dense in this verse.
plain_english: Although she is sung in many divisions, this Malini, beginning with na and ending with pha, is the primary one. She is the inner, uncontracted form of Bhairava, who is the mass of sound.
